events.outcome: CTExcel UK and its Back to China SIM Retention Plan are current. Community evidence repeatedly reports a 90-day activity rule for some no-plan accounts but also plan-dependent retention and conflicting post-plan behavior. The provider-visible pages do not cleanly expose current retention eligibility, price and post-expiry mechanics, so no universal lifecycle or annual keep cost is asserted.

data.acquisitionSummary: CTExcel UK remains a current EE-hosted UK-China mobile route with UK SIM bundles, annual China data plans and a provider-listed Back to China SIM Retention Plan. Current community reports include purchase and activation from China, with network/IP/eSIM friction in some cases.

keep.action: Provider currently exposes a Back to China SIM Retention Plan. Community evidence conflicts: some users report roughly 90-day activity for no-plan accounts while plan users follow plan-specific retention. Exact eligibility, current price and post-plan clock are not cleanly provider-reconciled, so no universal interval or annual cost is modeled.

data.chinaActivation: Current first-hand community reports show China-side purchase/activation and service use can work, but some users report UK-network/IP or eSIM setup friction. Treat China-first activation as operationally evidenced but not uniformly guaranteed.
data.kyc: Current provider pages reviewed here do not establish a universal identity/KYC rule for all CTExcel UK acquisition cohorts.
data.payment: Current official ordering/account paths exist; exact foreign-card acceptance and retention-plan payment execution were not independently normalized.
data.roamingSms: Current community evidence supports China-side signal, SMS/number use and support recovery. Service-specific OTP reliability and long-term roaming enforcement remain evidence-scoped.
data.refund: A 2026 first-hand signal-loss case reports fast official support recovery; broader replacement/refund outcomes remain unquantified.
data.holdReason: The provider confirms a current Back to China retention product, but exact eligibility, price and post-expiry rules are not cleanly extractable; community reports also conflict on no-plan 90-day activity versus plan-dependent retention.
data.tariffSummary: Current UK-China plans and retention service exist, but this review intentionally does not publish a single annual keep cost or universal 90-day lifecycle.
guideSteps: Choose the exact CTExcel plan/retention product before relying on any lifecycle rule.
Do not generalize a community 90-day activity report across plan cohorts.
Preserve China activation/support incidents and service-specific OTP outcomes as separate evidence.
